'''Werner Urland''' (born 13 April 1944) is a German chemist whose name is imprinted in the pioneering implementation of the [[Angular Overlap Model]] (AOM: a specific paradigm for accounting metal [[ion]]s in [[coordination complex|complexes]] or [[crystal]]s <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Schäffer | first1=Claus E. | last2=Jørgensen | first2=Chr. Klixbüll | title=The angular overlap model, an attempt to revive the ligand field approaches | journal=Molecular Physics | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=9 | issue=5 | year=1965 | issn=0026-8976 | doi=10.1080/00268976500100551 | pages=401–412| bibcode=1965MolPh...9..401S }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=Hoggard | first=Patrick E. | series=Structure and Bonding |title=Optical Spectra and Chemical Bonding in Inorganic Compounds| chapter=Angular Overlap Model Parameters | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | location=Berlin, Heidelberg | year=2004 | isbn=978-3-540-00853-8 | issn=0081-5993 | doi=10.1007/b11304 | pages=37–57|volume=106}}</ref><ref>T. Schönherr, M. Atanasov, H. Adamsky, Angular Overlap Model, in  A. B. P. Lever, J. A. McCleverty, T. J. Meyer (Eds.) Comprehensive coordination chemistry II, Vol. 2. Elsevier, Oxford, 2003, pp. 443-455.</ref>) for the interpretation of optical and magnetic properties of rare-earth [[coordination compound]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=On the ligand-field potential for f electrons in the angular overlap model | journal=Chemical Physics | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=14 | issue=3 | year=1976 | issn=0301-0104 | doi=10.1016/0301-0104(76)80136-x | pages=393–401| bibcode=1976CP.....14..393U }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=The application of the angular overlap model in the calculation of paramagnetic principal susceptibilities for f -electron systems | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=46 | issue=3 | year=1977 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(77)80627-1 | pages=457–460| bibcode=1977CPL....46..457U }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=The assessment of the crystal-field parameters for f<sup>n</sup>-electron systems by the angular overlap model rare-earth ions m<sup>3+</sup> in limf<sub>4</sub> and substituted in liyf<sub>4</sub> | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=77 | issue=1 | year=1981 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(81)85599-6 | pages=58–62| bibcode=1981CPL....77...58U }}</ref> This approach receives a renewed value in the context of the vogue around the [[lanthanide]]-based new materials, such as achieving [[magnet]]s at molecular scale,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Tang | first1=Jinkui | last2=Hewitt | first2=Ian | last3=Madhu | first3=N. T. | last4=Chastanet | first4=Guillaume | last5=Wernsdorfer | first5=Wolfgang | last6=Anson | first6=Christopher E. | last7=Benelli | first7=Cristiano | last8=Sessoli | first8=Roberta |author9-link=Annie K. Powell | last9=Powell | first9=Annie K. | title=Dysprosium Triangles Showing Single-Molecule Magnet Behavior of Thermally Excited Spin States | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=45 | issue=11 | date=6 March 2006 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.200503564 | pages=1729–1733| pmid=16496432 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Costes | first1=Jean-Pierre | last2=Dahan | first2=Françoise | last3=Wernsdorfer | first3=Wolfgang | title=Heterodinuclear Cu−Tb Single-Molecule Magnet | journal=Inorganic Chemistry | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=45 | issue=1 | year=2006 | issn=0020-1669 | doi=10.1021/ic050563h | pages=5–7| pmid=16390033 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cimpoesu | first1=Fanica | last2=Dahan | first2=Françoise | last3=Ladeira | first3=Sonia | last4=Ferbinteanu | first4=Marilena | last5=Costes | first5=Jean-Pierre | title=Chiral Crystallization of a Heterodinuclear Ni-Ln Series: Comprehensive Analysis of the Magnetic Properties. | journal=Inorganic Chemistry | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=51 | issue=21 | date=21 March 2012 | issn=0020-1669 | doi=10.1021/ic3001784 | pages=11279–11293| pmid=22435341 }}</ref>  or designing new [[phosphor]] materials.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Jüstel | first1=Thomas | last2=Nikol | first2=Hans | last3=Ronda | first3=Cees | title=New Developments in the Field of Luminescent Materials for Lighting and Displays | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=37 | issue=22 | date=4 December 1998 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/(sici)1521-3773(19981204)37:22<3084::aid-anie3084>3.0.co;2-w | pages=3084–3103| pmid=29711319 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Werner Urland was born in Berlin on 13 April 1944. Between 1963 and 1968 he studied and graduated in [[chemistry]] in [[Giessen]], Germany. The interval 1968-1971 was dedicated to the work of a doctoral [[thesis]], under the supervision of Professor R. Hoppe, on [[ternary compound|ternary]] [[oxide]]s of [[noble metal]]s. The [[PhD]] stage incorporated a scholarship at [[University College London|University College]] in [[London]], in the group of Dr. Malcolm Gerloch under the supervision of Professor Lord Jack Lewis ([[Jack Lewis, Baron Lewis of Newnham]], where the acquaintance with the magnetic properties and specific models of coordination compounds had defined a turning point in his career. The following post-doctoral stage (1971-1974) in preparative [[solid-state chemistry]] and the return to England, at [[Cambridge]], in the theory group directed by Prof. A. D. Buckingham, contoured an original composition of scientific interests, at the confluence of [[applied chemistry]] with the theoretical insight, aiming for understanding and predicting useful properties.
Assimilating the different formation sources, Werner Urland contoured his original perspective in the [[magnetochemistry]] of [[rare earth mineral|rare earth]] [[chemical compound|compounds]], the domain delineated by his habilitation treatise (1975-1980).

Between 1982 and 1986 he occupied a research position at the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] in [[Stuttgart]]. Since 1986 he has been appointed professor in [[Hanover]], where he acted till his retirement in 2007, on a chair dedicated to special topics of [[inorganic chemistry]]. In 1996 he declined an invitation to occupy a position as professor of inorganic chemistry at the [[University of Vienna]]. Since 2011, Werner Urland occupies a senior researcher position on grants, in the group of theoretical and [[computational chemistry]] of Professor Claude Daul, at [[University of Fribourg]], Switzerland. Presently, Werner Urland is dealing with setting up an institute in [[Muralto]]/[[Locarno]], Switzerland, with the help of the "Fondazione Sciaroni", dedicated to theoretical approach of material sciences and property design, thus supporting experimental work by universities and industries.

==Activity==

===Preparative solid state  and coordination chemistry===
In the branch dedicated to [[Solid-state chemistry|solid state chemistry]], Werner Urland et al. synthesized and characterized structurally, by [[X-ray crystallography]], several lanthanide-chalcogenide systems with unusual anionic structures, such as PrSe<sub>2</sub>, PrSe<sub>1.9−x</sub>, CeSe<sub>1.9−x</sub>  NdSe<sub>1.9 </sub>  <ref>{{cite journal|first1=P. |last1=Plambeck-Fischer|first2=W. |last2=Urland|first3=W. |last3=Abriel|journal=Zeitschrift für Kristallographie|year=1987|volume= 178|page=182|title=Synthesis of PrSe<sub>2</sub> and studies of single-crystal structure}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|first1=P.|last1=Plambeck-Fischer|first2=W.|last2=Urland|first3=W.|last3=Abriel|title=Crystal-structure of CeSe<sub>1.9−x</sub> and PreSe<sub>1.9−x</sub>|year=1988|volume=182 |page= 208|journal=Zeitschrift für Kristallographie}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Plambeck-Fischer | first1=P. | last2=Abriel | first2=W. | last3=Urland | first3=W. | title=Preparation and crystal structure of RESe<sub>1.9</sub> (RE=Ce, Pr) | journal=Journal of Solid State Chemistry | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=78 | issue=1 | year=1989 | issn=0022-4596 | doi=10.1016/0022-4596(89)90140-0 | pages=164–169| bibcode=1989JSSCh..78..164P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Plambeck-Fischer | first2=P. | last3=Grupe | first3=M. | title=Darstellung und Kristallstruktur von NdSe<sub>1.9</sub>|trans-title= Preparation and Crystal Structure of NdSe<sub>1.9</sub> |language=de| journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung B | publisher=Walter de Gruyter GmbH | volume=44 | issue=3 | date=1 March 1989 | issn=1865-7117 | doi=10.1515/znb-1989-0303 | pages=261–264| s2cid=98369397 | doi-access=free }}</ref> or more complex compositions, such as chalcogenide-silicates like  Nd<sub>2 </sub>SeSiO<sub>4 </sub> like M<sub> 4</sub>X<sub> 3</sub> [Si<sub>2 </sub>O<sub> 7</sub>] (M = Ce - Er; X = S, Se) <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grupe | first1=M. | last2=Urland | first2=W. | title=Darstellung und Kristallstruktur von Nd<sub>2</sub>SeSiO<sub>4</sub> |trans-title= Preparation and Crystal Structure of Nd<sub>2</sub>SeSiO<sub>4</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung B | publisher=Walter de Gruyter GmbH | volume=45 | issue=4 | date=1 April 1990 | issn=1865-7117 | doi=10.1515/znb-1990-0410 | pages=465–468| s2cid=97491520 |language=de| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grupe | first1=Matthias | last2=Lissner | first2=Falk | last3=Schleid | first3=Thomas | last4=Urland | first4=Werner | title=Chalkogenid-Disilicate der Lanthanoide vom Typ M<sub>4</sub>X<sub>3</sub>[Si<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>] (M = Ce-Er; X = S, Se) | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=616 | issue=10 | year=1992 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.19926161009 | pages=53–60 | language=de}}</ref> The crystal structures of prototypic chalcogenides of trivalent lanthanides, like Ln<sub>2</sub>Se<sub>3</sub> (Ln=Sm, Tb, Ho) were resolved.,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grundmeier | first1=Thorsten | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Zur Kristallstruktur von Tb<sub>2</sub>Se<sub>3</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=623 | issue=11 | year=1997 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.19976231113 | pages=1744–1746 | language=de| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=Werner | last2=Person | first2=Helmut | title=Zur Kristallstruktur von Ho<sub>2</sub>Se<sub>3</sub>|trans-title= On the Crystal Structure of Ho<sub>2</sub>Se<sub>3</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung B | publisher=Walter de Gruyter GmbH | volume=53 | issue=8 | date=1 August 1998 | issn=1865-7117 | doi=10.1515/znb-1998-0821 | pages=900–902| s2cid=100943831 }}</ref> treating also their polymorphic manifestations  <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grundmeier | first1=Thorsten | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Zur Polymorphie von Sm<sub>2</sub>Se<sub>3</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=621 | issue=11 | year=1995 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.19956211125 | pages=1977–1979 | language=de}}</ref> and the electronic structure.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grundmeier | first1=T. | last2=Heinze | first2=Th. | last3=Urland | first3=W. | title=On the electronic structure of new ternary selenides of samarium | journal=Journal of Alloys and Compounds | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=246 | issue=1–2 | year=1997 | issn=0925-8388 | doi=10.1016/s0925-8388(96)02466-8 | pages=18–20}}</ref>
Other solid phase systems such as lanthanide aluminium halides, LnAl<sub>3</sub>X<sub>12</sub> (with Ln = lanthanide trivalent ions in the La-Ho series and X= Cl, Br)  were considered as synthetic and structural problems.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hake | first1=D. | last2=Urland | first2=W. | title=Darstellung und Kristallstruktur von LnAl<sub>3</sub>Cl<sub>12</sub> (Ln = Tb, Dy, Ho) und thermischer Abbau zu LnCl<sub>3</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=586 | issue=1 | year=1990 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.19905860114 | pages=99–105 | language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hake | first1=Dietmar | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Darstellung und Kristallstruktur von LnAl<sub>3</sub>Br<sub>12</sub> (Ln = La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd) und thermischer Abbau zu LnBr<sub>3</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=613 | issue=7 | year=1992 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.19926130107 | pages=45–48 | language=de}}</ref>
Another area of Werner Urland's research was contoured around the special properties of condensed systems, such as [[superconductivity]] of mixed oxide compounds, 
<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Tietz | first2=F. | title=Superconductivity in the Bi-Sr-Mg-Cu-O system | journal=Materials Research Bulletin | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=24 | issue=4 | year=1989 | issn=0025-5408 | doi=10.1016/0025-5408(89)90032-9 | pages=489–492}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Heinrich | first1=A. | last2=Urland | first2=W. | title=The system Ba<sub>0.6</sub>K<sub>0.4−x</sub>Cs<sub>x</sub>BiO<sub>3</sub>: Superconductivity dependence of T<sub>c</sub> on the cesium content | journal=Solid State Communications | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=80 | issue=7 | year=1991 | issn=0038-1098 | doi=10.1016/0038-1098(91)90064-3 | pages=519–522| bibcode=1991SSCom..80..519H }}</ref>
or [[Ionic conductivity (solid state)|ionic conductivity]] and dynamics of  sodium and lanthanide ions in crystals like Na<sup>+</sup>/Ln<sup>3+</sup>-ß"-Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>  <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Köhler | first1=Joachim | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Ionic Conductivity in Na<sup>+</sup>/Pr<sup>3+</sup>–β"–Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Crystals | journal=Journal of Solid State Chemistry | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=127 | issue=2 | year=1996 | issn=0022-4596 | doi=10.1006/jssc.1996.0372 | pages=161–168}}</ref><ref>J. Köhler and W. Urland Angew. Chem. 109, 150 (1997)</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Köhler | first1=Joachim | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=On the Mobility of Trivalent Ions: Pr<sup>3+</sup> in Pr<sup>3+</sup>-β"-Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English | publisher=Wiley | volume=36 | issue=12 | date=3 February 1997 | issn=0570-0833 | doi=10.1002/anie.199700851 | pages=85–87}}</ref>
The same systems received attention also in the respect of their magnetic properties, in relation with the determinant structural factors.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Soetebier | first1=Frank | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Strukturchemische und magnetische Untersuchungen an Ho<sup>3+</sup>-β"-Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>(Ho<sub>0</sub>, <sub>5</sub>Mg<sub>0</sub>, <sub>5</sub>Al<sub>10</sub>, <sub>5</sub>O<sub>17</sub>) | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=628 | issue=3 | year=2002 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/1521-3749(200203)628:3<711::aid-zaac711>3.0.co;2-g | pages=711–714 | language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Soetebier | first1=Frank | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Structural Chemistry and Magnetism of Tb<sup>3+</sup>-β′′-Alumina (Tb<sub>0.46</sub>Al<sub>10.62</sub>Mg<sub>0.38</sub>O<sub>17</sub>) | journal=European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry | publisher=Wiley | volume=2002 | issue=7 | year=2002 | issn=1434-1948 | doi=10.1002/1099-0682(200207)2002:7<1673::aid-ejic1673>3.0.co;2-f | pages=1673–1676}}</ref> 
Among other approached special properties, one may mention the treatment of bipolaron absorption in Ba<sub>1−x</sub>K<sub>x</sub>BiO<sub>3</sub>  and   Ba<sub>0.6</sub>K<sub>0.4−x</sub>BiO<sub>3</sub>   materials.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rüscher | first1=C.H. | last2=Heinrich | first2=A. | last3=Urland | first3=W. | title=Bipolaron absorption in Ba<sub>1−x</sub>K<sub>x</sub>BiO<sub>3</sub> and Ba<sub>0.6</sub>K<sub>0.4 − x</sub>Cs<sub>x</sub>BiO<sub>3</sub> | journal=Physica C: Superconductivity | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=219 | issue=3–4 | year=1994 | issn=0921-4534 | doi=10.1016/0921-4534(94)90402-2 | pages=471–482| bibcode=1994PhyC..219..471R }}</ref>

===Modelling breakthroughs===
After a brief apprenticeship in applying standard versions of ligand field modelling to transition metal complexes, tackling  single-crystal polarized spectra and magnetic anisotropy of Ni(II) and Co(II) complexes in the less usual five-coordination states,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gerloch | first1=M. | last2=Kohl | first2=J. | last3=Lewis | first3=J. | last4=Urland | first4=W. | title=Single-crystal polarized spectrum and paramagnetic anisotropy of five-co-ordinate, square pyramidal cobalt(II) complexes | journal=Journal of the Chemical Society A: Inorganic, Physical, Theoretical | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | year=1970 | issn=0022-4944 | doi=10.1039/j19700003283 | pages=3269–3283}}</ref> Werner Urland conceived his own "trademark" devising a ligand-field potential for f [[electron]]s in the frame of Angular Overlap Model.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=On the ligand-field potential for f electrons in the angular overlap model | journal=Chemical Physics | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=14 | issue=3 | year=1976 | issn=0301-0104 | doi=10.1016/0301-0104(76)80136-x | pages=393–401| bibcode=1976CP.....14..393U }}</ref>
Immediate applications clarified the meaning of the parameters, taking rare-earth hydroxides and chlorides as case studies.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=The interpretation of the crystal field parameters for fn-electron systems by the angular overlap model. The rare-earth hydroxides | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=50 | issue=3 | year=1977 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(77)80363-1 | pages=445–450| bibcode=1977CPL....50..445U }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=The interpretation of the crystal field parameters for fn-electron systems by the angular overlap model. Rare-earth ions in LaCl<sub>3</sub> | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=53 | issue=2 | year=1978 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(78)85400-1 | pages=296–299| bibcode=1978CPL....53..296U }}</ref> Many papers developed in this domain were single authored, marking the original perspective of Werner Urland. Briefly, describing the situation of [[ligand field theory]], practically equivalent to [[crystal field theory]] pointing that this method is more popular, often invoked in qualitative respects, for transition metal systems (coordination and solid phase compounds)<ref>B. N. Figgis, M. A. Hitchman, Ligand Field Theory and its Applications, Wiley-VCH, New York, 2000</ref> while for f-elements (lanthanide and actinide compounds) it is regarded as a rather specialized field, due to somewhat more complicated technical stances.<ref>D. J. Newman, B. K. C. Ng, Crystal Field Handbook, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, 2000</ref> A conceptual drawback is the lack of chemical intuitiveness of the parameters of classical ligand field theories. There are several conventions, such as Wybourne or Stevens parameterizations  <ref>B. G. Wybourne, Spectroscopic Properties of Rare Earths, Wiley Interscience, New York, 1965</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Stevens | first=K W H | title=Matrix Elements and Operator Equivalents Connected with the Magnetic Properties of Rare Earth Ions | journal=Proceedings of the Physical Society. Section A | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=65 | issue=3 | date=1 March 1952 | issn=0370-1298 | doi=10.1088/0370-1298/65/3/308 | pages=209–215| bibcode=1952PPSA...65..209S | s2cid=98618693 }}</ref>  An alternate offer was identified in the Angular Overlap Model basically developed for d-type transition metal systems  <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Schäffer | first1=Claus E. | last2=Jørgensen | first2=Chr. Klixbüll | title=The angular overlap model, an attempt to revive the ligand field approaches | journal=Molecular Physics | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=9 | issue=5 | year=1965 | issn=0026-8976 | doi=10.1080/00268976500100551 | pages=401–412| bibcode=1965MolPh...9..401S }}</ref><ref>P. E. Hoggard, Struct. Bonding. 2004, 106, 37-57</ref><ref>T. Schönherr, M. Atanasov, H. Adamsky, Angular Overlap Model, in  A. B. P. Lever, J. A. McCleverty, T. J. Meyer (Eds.) Comprehensive coordination chemistry II, Vol. 2. Elsevier, Oxford, 2003, pp. 443-455.</ref> It is the merit of Werner Urland for stating the AOM version for f-type compounds, advocating for it by systematic applications acting as proof for the validity of this approach. 
The theoretical activity was complemented by involvement in synthetic coordination chemistry, producing new coordination compounds taken as relevant new case studies for ligand field interpretation of magnetic properties. A series consisting in individual octahedral units [LnCl<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3−</sup>,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=Werner | last2=Hallfeldt | first2=Jens | title=Synthese und Kristallstrukturen von (2-Methylpyridinium)<sub>3</sub>[TbCl<sub>6</sub>] und (2-Methylpyridinium)<sub>2</sub>[TbCl<sub>5</sub>(1-Butanol)] | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=626 | issue=12 | year=2000 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/1521-3749(200012)626:12<2569::aid-zaac2569>3.0.co;2-0 | pages=2569–2573 | language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hallfeldt | first1=Jens | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Synthese und Kristallstrukturen von (3-Methylpyridinium)<sub>3</sub>[DyCl<sub>6</sub>] und (3-Methylpyridinium)<sub>2</sub>[DyCl<sub>5</sub>(Ethanol)] | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=627 | issue=3 | year=2001 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/1521-3749(200103)627:3<545::aid-zaac545>3.0.co;2-z | pages=545–548| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hallfeldt | first1=Jens | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Synthese, Kristallstruktur und magnetisches Verhalten von (2,4,6-Trimethylpyridinium)<sub>10</sub>[ErCl<sub>6</sub>][ErCl<sub>5</sub>(H<sub>2</sub>O)]<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>3</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=628 | issue=12 | year=2002 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/1521-3749(200212)628:12<2661::aid-zaac2661>3.0.co;2-u | pages=2661–2664 | language=de}}</ref> is interesting by the intrinsic simplicity of these complexes, once is known that lanthanide complexes are usually adopting higher coordination numbers, the hexa-coordination being enforced  mostly by the doping regime, in solid lattices, such as elpasolites (a variety of [[Halide minerals]]  with ABM<sub>2</sub>X<sub>3 </sub>[[stoichiometry]]). The magnetic properties of [LnCl<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3−</sup> complexes (with [[pyridinium]] counter ions) were analysed in the non-trivial details of the causal role of the ligand field effects.  In the same spirit, a detailed attention was devoted to the relatively simple lanthanide pentakis nitrato complexes, starting from the synthesis stage  <ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=Preparation, crystal structure and magnetic properties of complex rare earth nitrates | journal=Journal of the Less Common Metals | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=93 | issue=2 | year=1983 | issn=0022-5088 | doi=10.1016/0022-5088(83)90199-6 | pages=431–432}}</ref> continued into the instrumental and theoretical characterization. The [[Electron paramagnetic resonance]] (EPR) spectra of the pentakis nitrato ytterbate(III), [Yb(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>  <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Kremer | first2=R. | title=Electron spin resonance spectra of low-symmetry rare-earth complexes: tetraphenylarsonium pentakis(nitrato)ytterbate(III) | journal=Inorganic Chemistry | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=23 | issue=11 | year=1984 | issn=0020-1669 | doi=10.1021/ic00179a017 | pages=1550–1553}}</ref>  was recorded and modelled, the ligand field treatment being based also on advanced neutron spectroscopy measurements.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Kremer | first2=R. | last3=Furrer | first3=A. | title=Crystal field levels in tetraphenylarsoniumpentakis(nitrato)ytterbate(III) determined by neutron spectroscopy | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=132 | issue=2 | year=1986 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(86)80090-2 | pages=113–115| bibcode=1986CPL...132..113U }}</ref>
A peculiar manifestation, discovered in the light of the developed methodologies, was the first report of level crossing in ligand field diagrams, tuned by external pressure.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Hochheimer | first2=H.D. | last3=Kourouklis | first3=G.A. | last4=Kremer | first4=R. | title=The first observation of a crossing of crystal-field levels | journal=Journal of the Less Common Metals | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=111 | issue=1–2 | year=1985 | issn=0022-5088 | doi=10.1016/0022-5088(85)90190-0 | page=221}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Hochheimer | first2=H.D. | last3=Kourouklis | first3=G.A. | last4=Kremer | first4=R. | title=Pressure-dependent crystal field splitting of Pr3+ in LaCl3: The observation of a crossing of crystal field levels | journal=Solid State Communications | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=55 | issue=7 | year=1985 | issn=0038-1098 | doi=10.1016/0038-1098(85)90831-2 | pages=649–651| bibcode=1985SSCom..55..649U }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Hochheimer | first2=H.D. | last3=Kourouklis | first3=G.A. | last4=Kremer | first4=R. | title=The first observation of a crossing of crystal field levels | journal=Physica B+C | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=139-140 | year=1986 | issn=0378-4363 | doi=10.1016/0378-4363(86)90647-9 | pages=553–554| bibcode=1986PhyBC.139..553U }}</ref>
A systematic attention was devoted to the magnetism determined by lanthanide ions in solid compounds like the ternary oxides,  CsLnO<sub>2</sub> <ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=Werner | title=Magnetische Eigenschaften der Normaltemperaturform von CsTmO2 / Magnetic Properties of the Normal-Temperature Form of CsTmO<sub>2</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung A | publisher=Walter de Gruyter GmbH | volume=34 | issue=8 | date=1 August 1979 | issn=1865-7109 | doi=10.1515/zna-1979-0813 | pages=997–1002| bibcode=1979ZNatA..34..997U | s2cid=96245048 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=Werner | title=Magnetische Eigenschaften der Normaltemperaturform von CsYbO<sub>2</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung A | publisher=Walter de Gruyter GmbH | volume=35 | issue=2 | date=1 January 1980 | issn=1865-7109 | doi=10.1515/zna-1980-0213 | pages=247–251| s2cid=96531405 | doi-access=free }}</ref> or Cs<sub>2</sub>MLnX<sub>6</sub> elpasolite type systems, with various combination of (M = Na, K, Rb) alkaline metal ions and (X=F, Cl, Br) halides, for several Ln(III) rare earth cases.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=W. | title=Magnetische Eigenschaften der Thuliumverbindungen Cs<sub>2</sub>MTmF<sub>6</sub> (M = Na, K, Rb) und Cs<sub>2</sub>KTmX<sub>6</sub> (X = Cl, Br) | journal=Berichte der Bunsengesellschaft für physikalische Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=83 | issue=10 | year=1979 | issn=0005-9021 | doi=10.1002/bbpc.19790831017 | pages=1042–1046}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Urland | first=Werner | title=Über des magnetische Verhalten von Cs<sub>2</sub>MYbF<sub>6</sub> (M = Na, K, Rb) und Cs<sub>2</sub>NaYbBr<sub>6</sub> |trans-title= On the Magnetic Behaviour of Cs<sub>2</sub>MYbF<sub>6</sub> (M = Na, K, Rb) and Cs<sub>2</sub>NaYbBr<sub>6</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung A | publisher=Walter de Gruyter GmbH | volume=34 | issue=12 | date=1 January 1979 | issn=1865-7109 | doi=10.1515/zna-1979-1218 | pages=1507–1511| s2cid=93923011 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Urland | first1=W. | last2=Feldner | first2=K. | last3=Hoppe | first3=R. | title=Über das Magnetische Verhalten von Cs<sub>2</sub>KPrF<sub>6</sub> und Cs<sub>2</sub>RbPrF<sub>6</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=465 | issue=1 | year=1980 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.19804650102 | pages=7–14 | language=de}}</ref> Werner Urland proved the ligand field as the determinant for the pattern of [[magnetic susceptibility]] dependences on temperature, often mistakenly attributed to inter-center exchange coupling.
A distinct branch of investigation concerned the unusual ferromagnetic Gd(III)-Gd(III) exchange coupling recorded in newly synthesized homo-polynuclear complexes of gadolinium with various carboxylates (acetate, fluoro- and chloro- substituted acetate) as bridging ligand.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hatscher | first1=Stephan T. | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Unexpected Appearance of Molecular Ferromagnetism in the Ordinary Acetate &#91;{Gd(OAc)3(H2O)2}2&#93;⋅4 H2O | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=42 | issue=25 | date=30 June 2003 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.200250738 | pages=2862–2864| pmid=12833342 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rohde | first1=Alexander | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Synthese und Kristallstrukturen von Ln(ClF<sub>2</sub>CCOO)<sub>3</sub>(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>3</sub> (Ln = Gd, Dy, Ho, Er) und magnetisches Verhalten von Gd(ClF<sub>2</sub>CCOO)<sub>3</sub>(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>3</sub> | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=630 | issue=13–14 | year=2004 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.200400173 | pages=2434–2437 | language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rohde | first1=Alexander | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | title=Synthese, Kristallstruktur und magnetisches Verhalten von [NH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>][Gd(Cl<sub>2</sub>HCCOO)<sub>4</sub>] | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=631 | issue=2–3 | year=2005 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.200400290 | pages=417–420 | language=de}}</ref>

==Recent advances==
Following the retirement in 2007 from Hannover professorship, Werner Urland resumed the scientific activity as guest senior researcher in the group of Professor Claude Daul at [[University of Fribourg]] ([[Switzerland]]), where he proposed a topic related to the so-called "Warm-White Light", namely the improvement of blue-type [[light-emitting diode]]s (LEDs) towards the better resemblance to the sunlight spectrum by coating with appropriate [[phosphor]]s based on lanthanide doped materials.  The topic represents a hot relevance in the context of the trends of eliminating traditional incandescent light bulbs, for the sake of energy saving new technologies . This technological challenge is underlined by the award of the 2014 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] "for the invention of efficient blue light-emitting diodes, which has enabled bright and energy-saving white light sources" to [[Shuji Nakamura]], [[Isamu Akasaki]] and [[Hiroshi Amano]] and by the declaration of 2015 as [[International Year of Light]] and Light-based Technologies, (IYL 2015). 
Hybridizing Werner's Urland expertise in experimental and theoretical aspects of rare earth materials with a computation and analysis methodology due to C. Daul and M. Atanasov,<ref>M. Atanansov, C. A. Daul and C. Rauzy, Struct. Bond., 2004, 106, 97</ref> altogether with methodological knowledge of external collaborators of the group, a series of works was produced, dealing with the analysis and prediction form first principles of the key factors in the [[luminescence]] of relevant lanthanide ions in various environments.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ramanantoanina | first1=Harry | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | last3=Cimpoesu | first3=Fanica | last4=Daul | first4=Claude | title=Ligand field density functional theory calculation of the 4f<sup>2</sup> → 4f<sup>1</sup>5d<sup>1</sup> transitions in the quantum cutter Cs<sub>2</sub>KYF<sub>6</sub>:Pr<sup>3+</sup> | journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | volume=15 | issue=33 | year=2013 | pages=13902–10 | issn=1463-9076 | doi=10.1039/c3cp51344k | pmid=23846586 | bibcode=2013PCCP...1513902R | url=http://www.repo.uni-hannover.de/handle/123456789/2203 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ramanantoanina | first1=Harry | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | last3=García-Fuente | first3=Amador | last4=Cimpoesu | first4=Fanica | last5=Daul | first5=Claude | title=Calculation of the 4f<sup>1</sup>→4f<sup>0</sup>5d<sup>1</sup> transitions in Ce<sup>3+</sup>-doped systems by Ligand Field Density Functional Theory | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=588 | year=2013 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/j.cplett.2013.10.012 | pages=260–266| bibcode=2013CPL...588..260R }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ramanantoanina | first1=Harry | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | last3=García-Fuente | first3=Amador | last4=Cimpoesu | first4=Fanica | last5=Daul | first5=Claude | title=Ligand field density functional theory for the prediction of future domestic lighting | journal=Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | volume=16 | issue=28 | year=2014 | issn=1463-9076 | doi=10.1039/c3cp55521f | pages=14625–14634| pmid=24855637 | bibcode=2014PCCP...1614625R | s2cid=24140789 | url=http://www.repo.uni-hannover.de/handle/123456789/163 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ramanantoanina | first1=Harry | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | last3=Cimpoesu | first3=Fanica | last4=Daul | first4=Claude | title=The angular overlap model extended for two-open-shell f and d electrons | journal=Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | volume=16 | issue=24 | year=2014 | issn=1463-9076 | doi=10.1039/c4cp01193g | pages=12282–12290| pmid=24819302 | bibcode=2014PCCP...1612282R | url=http://www.repo.uni-hannover.de/handle/123456789/164 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ramanantoanina | first1=Harry | last2=Urland | first2=Werner | last3=Herden | first3=Benjamin | last4=Cimpoesu | first4=Fanica | last5=Daul | first5=Claude | title=Tailoring the optical properties of lanthanide phosphors: prediction and characterization of the luminescence of Pr3+-doped LiYF4 | journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | volume=17 | issue=14 | year=2015 | issn=1463-9076 | doi=10.1039/c4cp05148c | pages=9116–9125| pmid=25759864 | bibcode=2015PCCP...17.9116R | doi-access=free }}</ref>
The modelling is based on a set of algorithmic steps abbreviated as LFDFT,<ref>M. Atanansov, C. A. Daul and C. Rauzy, Struct. Bond., 2004, 106, 97</ref>  consisting in non-routine calculations in the frame of [[density functional theory]] (DFT) followed by the analysis in the frame of [[ligand field theory]]. The issue of first principles calculations on rare-earth systems is non-trivial, because of special features of the f-shell, such as the shielded and weakly interacting nature, that poses technical and conceptual difficulties, in relation to modern methods of [[quantum chemistry]].<ref>M. Ferbinteanu, F. Cimpoesu and S. Tanase, Struct. Bond., 2015, 163, 185-230.</ref> The specific problem of the modelling the [[luminescence]] of rare-earth systems called the need of extending the ligand field phenomenology, from its one-shell status (dedicated to d or f electrons) to a two-shell [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian]], comprising simultaneously the d and f shells, because the involved optical transitions  have inter-shell nature. 
Also recently, Werner Urland, entered the terrain of actinide chemistry, explaining intriguing magnetic behaviour due strong ligand field on uranium(IV) ions in thiophosphates and silicates.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Neuhausen | first1=Christine | last2=Hatscher | first2=Stephan T. | last3=Panthöfer | first3=Martin | last4=Urland | first4=Werner | last5=Tremel | first5=Wolfgang | title=Comprehensive Uranium Thiophosphate Chemistry: Framework Compounds Based on Pseudotetrahedrally Coordinated Central Metal Atoms | journal=Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=639 | issue=15 | date=23 September 2013 | issn=0044-2313 | doi=10.1002/zaac.201300300 | pages=2836–2845}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Morrison | first1=Gregory | last2=Ramanantoanina | first2=Harry | last3=Urland | first3=Werner | last4=Smith | first4=Mark D. | last5=zur Loye | first5=Hans-Conrad | title=Flux Synthesis, Structure, Properties, and Theoretical Magnetic Study of Uranium(IV)-Containing A<sub>2</sub>USi<sub>6</sub>O<sub>15</sub>(A = K, Rb) with an Intriguing Green-to-Purple, Crystal-to-Crystal Structural Transition in the K Analogue | journal=Inorganic Chemistry | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=54 | issue=11 | date=15 May 2015 | issn=0020-1669 | doi=10.1021/acs.inorgchem.5b00556 | pages=5504–5511| pmid=25978501 | s2cid=197379214 }}</ref>
The whole deal underlines the validity and renewed value of Werner Urland's early ideas about the theoretical and practical aspects emerging from the chemistry and physics of f-elements.
